checks.rule: Time Stamped DSM is an Environment Agency archive of raster elevation surveys.
DSM data is produced from the last-return LIDAR signal.
DSM includes terrain plus above-ground objects such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
Available DSM resolutions include 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m depending on survey project.
DSM tiles are provided as GeoTIFF rasters in 5 km zip archives.
DSM elevations are metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid.
Environment Agency states LIDAR vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 cm RMSE.
Survey metadata identifies date, resolution, transformation and geoidal model.
Do not substitute DSM values for bare-earth DTM values in parcel terrain-height calculations.
A DSM-DTM difference can indicate surface objects but is not itself a parcel ground-height difference.
Quarantine samples where buildings or vegetation contaminate a metric intended to represent terrain only.
When DSM is used as a diagnostic, preserve matching survey epoch and grid provenance before comparing with DTM.
